solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: the direction a clock's hands travel, so a way of going that follows time itself

explanation.surface: A question of choosing the punctual route to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The direction followed by the hands of a clock is literally the timely way round, a playful cryptic description.

parts.note: lay means non-professional, amateur
out means left out, excluded

explanation.surface: An amateur has been left out of the planning.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement or design of a page, garden or building is its plan.

clue.text: Go in confused by commanding officer speaking softly

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of the words go in are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Someone goes in, flustered by a quietly spoken commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' here just means beside, not a sign of one piece going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves murmur gently, and lovers talking tenderly in low murmurs are said to be doing the same.

clue.text: First person in cape to see apparition

indicators.note: in means the first person pronoun is placed within the name of the cape

parts.note: Cape Wrath is the north-western tip of mainland Scotland
I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone is the first to visit a cape to see a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Wrath is a headland at the far north-west of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostly figure or spectre, especially one seen shortly before or after death.

parts.note: a schoolmaster whose subject involves experiments in the laboratory

explanation.surface: A question about a master of experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster who teaches chemistry, physics or biology spends lessons running experiments.

parts.note: to lounge is to idle or loaf about
bar as a preposition means save or except

explanation.surface: An instruction to idle away time and save space.
explanation.walkthrough: A lounge bar is the more comfortable room of a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The more comfortable public area in a British pub is one particular kind of room.

parts.note: fed up reads as fed while sitting raised up, not as annoyed

explanation.surface: Asking where a baby gets fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' suggests a cross baby, but it means fed while raised up off the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall seat with a tray on which a baby sits elevated at mealtimes.

parts.note: read as a period of life when one is soft rather than tough

explanation.surface: An exclamation that this is not the moment for hardness.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says now is not the time for toughness; cryptically, the soft (not tough) time is the period of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Early youth, when someone is young and immature, is a soft period of life.

clue.text: These men and women can be found in force

definitions.text: These men and women can be found in force

parts.words: These men and women can be found in force
parts.note: officers serving together in a constabulary, which is called a force

explanation.surface: People appearing in large numbers somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in force' seems to mean in great numbers, but it is the name for a constabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers of the law serve in what is called a force, the organised body of constables.

clue.text: Impulse to do some light criminal work?

definitions.text: Impulse to do some light criminal work?

parts.words: Impulse to do some light criminal work?
parts.note: light reads as setting fire, so criminal fire-raising rather than minor wrongdoing

explanation.surface: An urge to commit some petty offences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like minor, but it is setting alight: the urge is to commit arson.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive compulsion to set fires, a criminal act of lighting things.

parts.note: afoot read as on the foot: no shoes are worn

explanation.surface: A remark that nothing is happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' seems to mean going on, but read as on the foot it describes bare feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Without shoes, having nothing on one's feet, especially said of a horse lacking its iron.

parts.note: turns means changes, as milk turns
tone is the quality or character of a sound

explanation.surface: A bird alters the pitch of its song.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wading shorebird that flips over stones looking for food.

parts.note: stock read as farm animals, kept from roaming by a rope or chain

explanation.surface: Regulators limit trading in shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' suggests stock-market trading, but it is livestock tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or chain tying an animal to a post limits how far grazing livestock can wander.

definitions.meaning: there is still space left, as in a room yet to be taken
a storeroom in a large house for preserves, cordials and cakes

explanation.walkthrough: A still room was originally where cordials were distilled in a country house, later a housekeeper's pantry.
explanation.definitionFit: Space that remains available, and also a household storeroom where preserves and drinks were made.

clue.text: Attack a good man in charge who is pompous

parts.note: to bomb is to attack from the air
ST, for saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a decent manager who is self-important.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated, high-sounding speech or manner is grandiloquent and self-important.

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A deal is struck with a Frenchman to create a new treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal arrangement between parties, a treaty or understanding.

indicators.note: not all means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: seem means appear

explanation.surface: Not everyone shows up to see the announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something is to notice or observe it.

clue.text: Way academician goes to terminus briefly

parts.note: ST, for street, is a way
A is an abbreviation for academician, as in RA

explanation.surface: A Royal Academy member takes a road to the railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' marks the definition as an abbreviation: a terminus is a station, shortened to STA.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is a railway station, and STA is the standard shortening of station.

indicators.note: at regular intervals means take every second letter of the name

explanation.surface: A matter of timing before someone named George.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word meaning prior to, earlier than.

parts.note: thought means considered
reading means studying, as at university

explanation.surface: Someone thought about taking telepathy as a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathy is the supposed ability to perceive other people's minds directly.

parts.note: finished a fast by eating: having a meal ends a fast

explanation.surface: Asking whether something was completed quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like quickly, but it is abstaining from food, ended by a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Consuming a meal brings a fast to an end, so having eaten is to have ended fasting.

clue.text: Be bold perhaps having aimed high

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be differently arranged

explanation.surface: Being daring might involve setting your sights high.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball sent in a high arc over an opponent was aimed high.

clue.text: Old boy left before one, say, getting up to do a favour

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means the abbreviation is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: An old boy leaves before someone gets out of bed to help.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to accommodate them, doing them a kindness.

clue.text: Coming from America, not Australian but European peninsula

indicators.note: coming from means the letters are drawn out of the word America and reworked

explanation.surface: Someone travels from America, not Australia, to a European peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes one A from AMERICA, and 'Coming from' rearranges the remaining MERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula jutting into the Black Sea, south of Ukraine.

clue.text: Accountant left one company cotton cloth

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An accountant left a firm dealing in cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-woven cotton fabric, often printed.

clue.text: Locals at home holding a wild person

parts.note: a local is a pub, and two pubs give bar and bar

indicators.note: holding means the word for at home contains the letter

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Pubgoers at home are keeping a savage.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'local' is one's regular pub, so 'Locals' gives two bars.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncivilised, savage or brutish person.

clue.text: Carry on again about birds on the way back

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: on the way back means the flightless birds are read backwards

parts.note: emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: Restarting a journey with birds as you return.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up again after a pause is to carry on once more.

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: splashing suggests the letters of Lima are scattered about

explanation.surface: Spilling tea in the Peruvian capital onto armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Protective armour made of interlinked metal rings.

clue.text: Get acquainted with position — the map's right

definitions.meaning: to find one's bearings, to get familiar with one's surroundings
east, which lies on the right of a conventionally drawn map

explanation.walkthrough: On a map with north at the top, the east lies to the right, and the East is called the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding one's bearings is to orient oneself, and the East lies to the right side of a map.

clue.text: One of the fraternity's forenames rewritten

indicators.note: rewritten indicates the letters of the word are put down in a new order

explanation.surface: A member of the brotherhood has had their first names changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the secretive fraternal society, the Brotherhood of Masons.
